summary: Web-based app that loads real BTC historical data (free endpoint) and displays an interactive monthly candlestick chart with automated, dynamic liquidity level detection (horizontal lines + wick-based liquidity boxes) using consecutive opposite candle and breakout structure logic, including invalidation and cleanup rules.
architectural_notes: Use a fast free public market data source (no API keys) for BTC/USD or BTC/USDT monthly OHLCV.
Timeframe is Monthly (1M) only for now; liquidity logic is designed specifically for 1M.
Improve BTC OHLCV data fetching robustness (handle endpoint outages/CORS/network failures) and switch to a more reliable free no-API-key data source chosen for speed/stability.
known_issues: BTC chart page shows 'failed to fetch data' error (started recently).

existing_features.title: Fetch real BTC historical monthly OHLCV data from a fast free public endpoint (no API key) and expose it to the frontend in a stable format suitable for charting.
Render a fully interactive monthly (1M) candlestick chart and lock the UI to the Monthly timeframe (no timeframe switching).

Implement automated horizontal liquidity line detection and lifecycle on the monthly chart: (a) draw the initial horizontal line at the lower wick (low) of the first available monthly candle; (b) detect 'two consecutive opposite candles' against the current move and, when detected, draw a new horizontal line at the wick of the first opposite candle; (c) when price breaks a horizontal line, wait for the next two consecutive opposite candles and draw a new horizontal line at the wick of the first opposite candle; (d) keep only the most structurally relevant levels as the structure shifts forward.

Implement wick-based liquidity zone boxes (primary liquidity zones) derived from reversal structures, including the 'upper liquidity logic': (a) after detecting a reversal structure, compute the relevant wick range and draw a semi-transparent box that extends forward in time; (b) when a small opposite move forms inside a larger trend and then trend resumes, mark BOTH liquidity areas (at start of opposite candles and at end where trend resumes) using wick-based boxes; (c) manage both upper and lower liquidity zones using the same active/inactive logic.

Implement liquidity box invalidation and cleanup rules: (a) remove a box when price touches it AND then clearly moves away; (b) keep a box active if only 1–3 candles interact inside it and price is still moving inside/around it; (c) remove a box if it was touched long ago and price moved significantly far away and many candles formed since; (d) for upper liquidity, if price breaks above upper liquidity and fully clears it, remove that upper box; (e) inactive boxes must automatically disappear from the chart.

Apply visual styling for professional smart-money liquidity visualization: thin clean horizontal lines; semi-transparent liquidity boxes; distinct colors for active vs inactive (if an intermediate inactive state is shown); keep the chart visually clean by removing invalidated levels/zones.
Create and apply a coherent visual theme for the app (colors, typography, spacing, layout) that fits a financial charting tool aesthetic and is enforced consistently across the UI.

Replace the current CoinGecko-based monthly candle fetch (daily aggregation) with a faster and more reliable free public endpoint (no API key) that can return BTC monthly (1M) OHLCV directly, while keeping the frontend Candle format stable for charting.

Add resilient client-side fetching behavior for monthly candles to prevent intermittent endpoint failures from breaking the BTC chart page (timeout/abort, clearer error classification, and fallback to a secondary free public endpoint if the primary fails).
Update loading/error UI copy on the BTC chart page so it does not mention a specific provider (e.g., CoinGecko) and instead references “market data” generically.
